newsitem.title: GERMANY: German car production up 4 pct in 1996 - report.
newsitem.headline: German car production up 4 pct in 1996 - report.

text.p: German carmakers increased production in 1996 by around four percent to 4.54 million cars, but will face a challenging year in 1997, the head of the VDA German Car Association told a German newspaper on Thursday.
Bernd Gottschalk told the Handelsblatt newspaper that strong export demand that helped sales in 1996 may not continue.
"Extremely helpful export developments will probably not be repeated," he told the newspaper in an interview.
German 1996 truck production, meanwhile, was little changed at around 310,000.
Gottschalk said that although demand may be weak, new models hitting the market this year should lift production, even if only by a small amount.
"The heart of the question in the coming year is if we can succeed in moderate growth of at least two percent," he said.

German carmakers, he went on, are likely to lift investment by around five percent in 1997, a smaller increase than in 1996 when the companies invested 14 billion marks ($9 billion) in their plants, an increase of 20 percent.
